fields.field: Cathode HF decoupling, deliberately SMALL. AZ431-A Figure 15 (stability boundary vs load capacitance, VKA=VREF curve) shows two stable regions with an unstable band between them; at our ~1.6 mA cathode current the lower stable region runs to roughly 10 nF. 1 n sits well inside it. The bulk capacitance is C10, held OFF the cathode by R31 on purpose -- DO NOT move a microfarad-scale cap onto this node, and do not raise this value, without re-reading that figure. Chart reading, not a specified number: confirm on the bench before release

fields.field: Q1 VGS clamp, K to the PMOS source; 10V SOD-123. Was a 12V BZT52C12, whose GUARANTEED max VZ of 12.7 V at 5 mA (DS18004) exceeds the DMP3130L +/-12 V VGSS absolute maximum -- the old part never bounded VGS. Vishay doc 86342 gives BZT52C10 as 9.50/10/10.50 V at IZT 5 mA with aVZ +5..+8 mV/C. VZ rises with current, so VZ(30 uA) <= VZ(5 mA) <= 10.50 V; at +85 C the bound is 10.50 + 0.008*60 = 10.98 V, inside 12 V with ~1.0 V margin. Cold end: 9.50 - 0.52 = 8.98 V, still far above Q1 threshold. Clamp dissipation at 15 V in is (15-10.5)/100k = 45 uA, 0.5 mW in a 410 mW part

fields.field: FITTED 0R LINK, deliberately not a DNP placeholder -- it sits in SERIES in the only supply path to the ring, so leaving it unpopulated would open the heater feed and the heater would never run at all. It reserves the position for a protective device against a fault path that is NEW: with RH1/RH2 sitting in the main-board branch and NOT in the fork feed, nothing limits the fork itself, so a short between the fork fingers -- which run at 0.20 mm clearance to a metal cell can, RING-PCB.md section 1 -- puts +12V_SW across Q2 unlimited, and possibly 12 V onto the cell. DO NOT FIT AS DRAWN: a PPTC is likely the wrong device here, because F1's own note records IH derating to 0.36 A at 85 C, and a part that holds the heater's 83 mA at pile temperature would nuisance-trip. The land exists so the option is not designed out; size it once the ring's resistance is fixed. A PPTC is likely the wrong device: F1's own note records IH derating to 0.36 A at 85 C for a 0.75 A part, so one holding the heater's 83 mA would nuisance-trip at pile temperature

fields.field: Solder lands at the tips of the two fork fingers, carrying the heater pair forward to a perpendicular ring PCB (a soldered T-joint, the way any right-angle daughterboard mounts). REPLACES the two edge castellations of Heater_Ring_Solder_Lands, which HEATED-SPREADER.md section 0 showed are orphaned by the end-window head. One finger per net, both layers of each finger paralleled. RING-PCB.md section 1 offered 4 conductors; only 2 are used, because Fab dropped the ring's temperature sensor from this revision -- the second layer of each finger stays physically free, so a v2 ring can add one with NO main-board change. FOOTPRINT IS DRAFT: RING-PCB.md section 5.1 forbids freezing the 0.6 mm finger width before the printed ASA neck bore is measured on a real part

fields.field: Isolates C10's bulk capacitance from the AZ431 cathode, which is what keeps the shunt out of its unstable band (see C9). It was originally the OPA2333's capacitive-load isolation and happens to be exactly right here -- note it would have been WRONG for a series reference like the REF33xx, which requires 0.1-10 uF ON its output pin. The 26.9 uA drawn by R34/R35 across 47R is a 1.25 mV offset that does not matter: it lands on VREF_TRIM, which is BOTH the LMP91000 bias reference and the ADS1119 external reference, so it cancels ratiometrically. Net name VREF_TRIM is retained despite there no longer being a trimmer -- firmware/src/lmp91000.h and firmware/tools/gen_hw_contract.py key off it

fields.field: Both halves are now unity-gain electrometer followers on the cell nodes: A buffers WE, B buffers RE and drives both the guard (through R40) and the ADC bias telemetry. Half A was freed by deleting the VREF trim divider. NO FEMTOAMPERE PART IS NEEDED HERE and this is the reason: SBOS351E gives OPA333 IB as +/-70 pA typ and +/-200 pA max at 25 C. MIND THE ARITHMETIC: IB is the AVERAGE of the two inputs, and a follower's electrode sees the non-inverting input alone, so the real bound is |IB| + |IOS|/2 = 200 + 200 = 400 pA. The RE node is ALREADY loaded by the LMP91000's own RE pin at +/-90 pA typ and +/-900 pA max over -40..80 C (SNAS506I IRE, TI's own front-page feature; at this board's 3.3 V the applicable column is nearer 800 pA). So half B takes RE's worst case from ~900 pA to ~1300 pA, +44%, and an ADA4530-1 at 20 fA would still leave ~900 pA and buy nothing. UNSTATED ASSUMPTION, flagged deliberately: SBOS351E gives NO max for IB over temperature, only +/-150 pA typ, so the claim that a chopper's charge-injection-dominated bias stays flat to 75 C rests on Figure 8, a typical curve, not a guaranteed limit. See POTTING.md section 1.3 under ../../../ha/farming/compostlab/o2-probe/

fields.field: 2.5 V reference, wired as a two-terminal shunt (REF strapped to the cathode). REPLACES the deleted R20 / RV1 / R21 trim divider: POTTING.md section 1.2 (../../../ha/farming/compostlab/o2-probe/) requires the cell to be swappable with the board potted, so no adjustable part may set the bias. AZ431-A datasheet Rev 3.4: B grade is the 0.4% bin, 2.490/2.500/2.510 V, and deviation over -40..85 C is 4.5 mV typ / 10 mV max, so the worst-case window is 2.480..2.520 V. PACKAGE PIN MAP IS NOT THE TI ONE -- N package is 1 REF, 2 CATHODE, 3 ANODE, where TI's TL431DBZ is 1 K, 2 REF, 3 A; see the symbol comment. Biased from +5V_ANALOG through R41 and NOT from 3V3A: the part needs IKA >= 1.0 mA (recommended operating conditions) and 3V3A leaves only 3.234 - 2.510 = 0.724 V of headroom, about 6% margin over that minimum, where +5V_ANALOG leaves 2.5 V
